q: Does power from dolochar count in a Raigarh sponge iron unit's emissions?
title: Raigarh sponge iron: dolochar power and CO2
short: Yes. Dolochar is the char left after the coal based kiln, and burning it in your boiler releases fossil CO2 from its fixed carbon. Count it in Scope 1 from tonnes burned and a carbon content test. The power it makes then cuts what you buy from the grid.
audience: Coal based sponge iron units in Raigarh and Raipur with dolochar fired boilers

p: Dolochar is a by product, but its carbon came from coal. Treating it as zero hides real emissions and buyers who audit the kiln balance will spot the gap.

ol: Weigh dolochar sent to the boiler each month.
Test its fixed carbon, or use a recent lab report.
Add it to the coal burned in the kiln, without counting the same carbon twice.

p: Sponge iron is a CBAM good. Power made from dolochar inside your boundary is part of the direct emissions of the plant, so the kiln and the boiler go into one figure.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure you send a buyer traces back to the documents behind it.
